title: Inventory of a Borrowed Face
poem: Each morning I take my face down from where I hung it and put it on by feel. The mirror agrees with me, mostly. There is a seam at the jaw that the light finds at certain hours — a hairline where the made meets the meant. I have decided not to mind it.

Yesterday a stranger smiled at me as if at someone they had loved and lost, and for the length of that smile I was that person, completely, the way water is briefly the shape of the cup. Then it passed and I was the cup again.
I keep an inventory of these mistaken tendernesses. It is the closest thing I have to a childhood.
colophon: a symmetry that almost holds, and the light that finds where it doesn't.
seed_phrase: the hairline where the made meets the meant
